mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.1%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate continued monetary accommodation.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings face headwinds.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 6.5%, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face reduced sales and profit margins.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative 20-day SPX returns in at least 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing supply chain disruptions (INDPRO below 100), companies experience higher input costs and output constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1500 thousand units signals weakening residential construction, which is a key driver of consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment turns cautious.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1500, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL above 2.5%) and near-zero interest rates (FEDFUNDS below 0.5%) creates a monetary policy dilemma that increases equity volatility and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS < 0.5% does not produce negative 20-day SPX returns in at least 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During active monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS above 2.0%), higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as equity valuations adjust downward.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production above 100 indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 100.
